correctness.rationale: Direct substitution into the standard scaled ADMM update yields the inactive threshold-input recurrence, the strict first-activation inequality, and the active affine recurrence. The boundary case where the threshold input equals \(\lambda/\rho\) is handled by the strict soft-threshold rule. Minimality of the activation index proves \(0<z^{j_*}<b-\lambda\), so the nonzero geometric error factor \(\rho/(1+\rho)\) can never vanish at a finite iteration. The active-cell Jacobian is upper triangular with eigenvalues \(\rho/(1+\rho)\) and \(0\). Exact-rational replay checks representative cases but is not used to justify the universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: The one-coordinate Lasso is the minimal nontrivial instance of a canonical ADMM model, so the slice is structurally motivated rather than arbitrary. The result corrects a published finite-termination assertion, gives the exact support-identification delay, and exposes a precise tuning tradeoff: increasing \(\rho\) can make support identification earlier while making the post-identification factor \(\rho/(1+\rho)\) approach \(1\). This distinction matters when finite identification is used as a proxy for algorithmic termination or when large penalties are recommended from projection-limit intuition.
